title: Covered calls harvest the volatility risk premium, not volatility
summary: A covered call program harvests the volatility risk premium: the gap between implied and realized volatility. It is like the equity risk premium that investors are paid for owning stocks. The speaker's VAY metric puts that premium in dollars and normalizes it by realized volatility so you can compare names on equal terms.

steps.caption: The stock you write calls on.
Realized volatility: how much it actually moved.
Implied volatility: the price of the call you sell.
The risk premium is implied minus realized. Rich when the gap is large; cheap when it is small or negative.
Normalize the premium by realized volatility to compare different stocks.

takeaways: Covered calls earn the volatility risk premium.
The premium is implied minus realized volatility.
Normalize it to compare names fairly.
caveats: VAY is the speaker's own metric; its method and results are not verified here. Link in bio is promotional.
